# What do I give my own markup depth and motion with?

Read this when your own markup casts a shadow, lifts under the pointer or runs a transition.

A shadow role names the depth a surface casts, and a motion role names how long a change runs and the curve it follows. The steps are on [the motion page](../scales/motion-and-layers.md).

<!-- @tree GENERATED by bun run generate:token-tree. Edit that script, not this copy. -->

| role | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `--dur-hover` | How long a hover or press response takes |
| `--dur-state` | How long a state change the user follows takes: a switch travelling to its other end, a progress bar reaching a new value, an onboarding dot widening to mark the step it is on |
| `--ease-hover` | The curve a hover or press response travels, and the other half of dur-hover: one says how long the answer takes and this says what it feels like on the way |
| `--ease-state` | The curve of a state change the user follows, paired with dur-state the way ease-hover is paired with dur-hover |
| `--lift-control` | How far a control rises under the pointer, which by default is nowhere |
| `--press-scale` | How far a control sinks under the pointer while it is held, and the other half of lift-control: that one says how far a control rises, this says how far it goes down |
| `--shadow-control-raised` | What a control rises to under the pointer |
| `--shadow-control-rest` | The depth a control carries at rest, which by default is none, for the reason given at shadow-surface-rest: the property has to be painted before a value can move it |
| `--shadow-surface-deep` | The depth of a surface that commands the screen, whether by covering it (a dialog, a sheet, a command palette, a coachmark) or by being the only thing on it (the sign-in card) |
| `--shadow-surface-floating` | The depth a surface carries AT REST because it floats over the page: a menu, a toast, a tooltip, a bulk action bar, a card's floating variant |
| `--shadow-surface-rest` | The depth a surface carries at rest when it is part of the page rather than floating over it, which by default is none |

<!-- @tree end -->
